titleText.es: Ese tema ('Battle Without Honor or Humanity') --al igual que 'La cabalgata de las valquirias'-- mejora *cualquier* actividad.
titleText.en: That track ('Battle Without Honor or Humanity') -- like 'Ride of the Valkyries' -- improves *any* activity.
titleText.noteEn: The title text names the Kill Bill track imagined in the final bubble and compares its dramatic effect with another famous piece used for battle scenes.

regions.labelEs: PASO MUCHO TIEMPO COREOGRAFIANDO MENTALMENTE ELABORADAS ESCENAS DE LUCHA CON LOS EXTRAÑOS QUE ME RODEAN.

applications.explanationEn: Paso matches the speaker, mucho tiempo gives the amount spent, and coreografiando names the ongoing activity with its -ando ending.
Que connects extraños to the added description built around rodean; me identifies the person those strangers surround.

regions.labelEs: VALE, SI ESE ANCIANO SACA UNA BALLESTA,

applications.exampleEs: SI ESE ANCIANO SACA UNA BALLESTA
applications.explanationEn: Si introduces the full genuinely possible condition, and saca uses the ordinary present form for the old man pulling out a crossbow rather than a future-tense form.

regions.labelEs: LE TIRO LA BALANZA POSTAL Y SALTO HACIA ATRÁS DETRÁS DE LA MÁQUINA DE SELLOS.

applications.explanationEn: Hacia and atrás combine to give the backward direction of the jump.

applications.exampleEs: DETRÁS DE LA MÁQUINA DE SELLOS
applications.explanationEn: Detrás de gives the relative location, and la máquina de sellos supplies the complete reference object.

regions.labelEs: PERO ¿Y SI LA MUJER DE LA PUERTA TIENE UNA KATANA EN ESA CAJA?

applications.exampleEs: Y SI LA MUJER DE LA PUERTA TIENE UNA KATANA EN ESA CAJA
applications.explanationEn: ¿Y si...? opens a new possibility for consideration, and the following present-time clause supplies that complete imagined possibility.

regions.labelEs: MEJOR PONGO EL TEMA DE LUCHA DE "KILL BILL" EN EL IPOD, POR SI ACASO.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the unchanged English proper title of a film, not Spanish vocabulary.
This is the unchanged product name iPod, not a Spanish vocabulary item.

applications.explanationEn: Mejor presents the safer decision, and pongo is the speaker's present form for the action chosen.
The three words form the fixed precaution expression used for an uncertain possibility.

cards.noteEn: Pasar can mean spending time when it is followed by a period or amount of time. Paso is the present form for the speaker.

cards.promptEs: pasar + cantidad de tiempo + verbo en -ando/-iendo
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone spends a period of time doing an activity?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of pasar, name the amount of time, and add the activity verb ending in -ando or -iendo.
cards.noteEn: Pasar changes to match who spends the time: paso, pasas, pasa, and so on. The activity uses the ongoing-action form: estudiar becomes estudiando and leer becomes leyendo.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”
Extraño can describe something as strange, but used as a noun for people it means strangers—people one does not know.

cards.questionEn: How do you add information about a named person or thing using “who,” “that,” or “which”?
cards.answerEn: Put que after the person or thing, then add a verb and the information about it.
cards.noteEn: Que links the added description to the person or thing before it. It does not change for masculine, feminine, singular, or plural nouns. The added part needs a verb: la casa que vimos means “the house that we saw.”

example.es: La casa que vimos es azul.
example.en: The house that we saw is blue.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.
Ese points to a masculine singular noun that is not presented as right next to the speaker. Feminine singular is esa.

example.en: I do not recognize that sound.

cards.answerEn: at him; marks the target of the throw
cards.noteEn: With tirar una cosa a alguien, le can point to the person toward whom the object is thrown. A fuller phrase beginning with a can clarify that person.

example.es: Le tiré la pelota a Pablo.
example.en: I threw the ball to Pablo.

cards.noteEn: After a noun, postal describes something belonging to or used by the mail service, such as una balanza postal or un código postal.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that movement, direction, or progress goes backward?
cards.noteEn: Hacia supplies the direction and atrás points toward the back or reverse. The phrase can describe physical movement or an abstract process.
Detrás is followed by de before the person or thing used as the reference point.

example.es: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
example.en: The garden is behind the house.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something is behind a person or object?
cards.answerEn: Use detrás de before the person or object used as the reference point.
cards.noteEn: Keep de after detrás. Before a pronoun, use forms such as detrás de mí, detrás de ti, or detrás de él; do not use the subject forms yo or tú after de.

example.es: El coche está detrás de la casa.
example.en: The car is behind the house.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes detrás de, “behind”
cards.noteEn: Use de after detrás and before the reference point. The two words work together as detrás de.

example.es: La mochila está detrás de mí.

cards.noteEn: At the start of ¿y si...?, y helps introduce another possibility for someone to consider rather than simply joining two items with ‘and.’

cards.questionEn: How do you ask someone to consider “what if” a possibility happens?
cards.answerEn: Begin with ¿y si...? and state the possibility with an ordinary verb form.
cards.noteEn: The opening y does not merely mean ‘and’ here. Together with unaccented si, it presents a possible situation for consideration. It can introduce a suggestion or a worry.

example.en: What if we take the train?

cards.noteEn: Si has no accent when it introduces the possibility after y. Together, ¿y si...? asks someone to consider what might happen.

cards.answerEn: by; at (identifying someone by a place)
cards.noteEn: A phrase with de can identify a person by the place associated with them. Context makes the relation spatial rather than ownership.

example.es: Habla con el hombre de la entrada.
example.en: Talk to the man by the entrance.

cards.answerEn: I'd better; it is better to
cards.noteEn: Placed before a present-time verb, mejor can introduce the course of action the speaker decides is wiser or safer.

cards.questionEn: How can you say that you had better choose a particular action?
cards.answerEn: Put mejor before a present-time verb that states the wiser action.
cards.noteEn: Spanish can omit a phrase such as será and begin directly with mejor. The subject is often clear from the verb: mejor llamo is ‘I'd better call,’ while mejor llamamos is ‘we'd better call.’

cards.answerEn: I put on; I start playing
cards.noteEn: Pongo is the irregular present form of poner for the speaker. With music or a recording, poner commonly means putting it on or starting it.

example.en: I put on music while I cook.

cards.noteEn: Tema can mean a topic, but in music it can name a recognizable melody or theme.

example.es: Reconocí el tema de la película.

cards.promptEs: Kill Bill · tema de lucha · Battle Without Honor or Humanity
cards.answerEn: The imagined soundtrack is the dramatic track “Battle Without Honor or Humanity,” prominently used in Kill Bill.
cards.noteEn: The comic's title text names the track and jokes that, like “Ride of the Valkyries,” it makes any ordinary activity feel like a cinematic confrontation.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins por si acaso, ‘just in case’
cards.noteEn: Por is fixed inside the three-word precaution expression por si acaso.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that you take a precaution “just in case”?
cards.answerEn: Use por si acaso after the precaution.
cards.noteEn: Por si acaso is a fixed expression for preparing for something uncertain. A shorter por si + clause can name the possibility directly, as in por si llueve, ‘in case it rains.’

example.en: I'm bringing money just in case.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; middle of por si acaso, ‘just in case’
cards.noteEn: Si remains unaccented inside por si acaso. The whole expression introduces a precaution for an uncertain possibility.

example.es: Trae una chaqueta por si acaso.
example.en: Bring a jacket just in case.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes por si acaso, ‘just in case’
cards.noteEn: Acaso completes the fixed precaution expression. This is different from acaso used by itself to add doubt to a question.

example.es: Guarda una copia por si acaso.
example.en: Keep a copy just in case.
